get_airport_status.description: Check one US airport with the FAA: whether it has a ground stop, a ground delay program, arrival or departure delays, a closure or deicing right now, with the reason, how long the delays are and when it should end, plus the runways in use. An airport with nothing going on comes back as 'No delays' rather than failing the step.

get_airport_status.name: get_airport_status

parameters.description: The airport to check: pick one of the FAA's major airports, or type any US airport's three-letter code (ATL) or its ICAO code starting with K (KATL).

examples.label: Chicago O'Hare, by its ICAO code

parameters.name: airport

airport_code.description: The airport's three-letter FAA code, e.g. 'ATL'.

airport_name.description: The airport's name. Empty when the FAA lists nothing there, since its name comes with its events.

arrival_rate.description: How many arrivals an hour the airport is accepting. Given only while the airport has an event.

arrival_runways.description: The runways landing aircraft are using, e.g. '17C/17L'. Given only while the airport has an event.

departure_runways.description: The runways departing aircraft are using, e.g. '18R/17R'. Given only while the airport has an event.

event_count.description: How many events the FAA lists there.

events.description: Every event at the airport, most disruptive first.

advisory_url.description: For a ground stop or delay program, the link to the FAA's advisory with its full details.

airport_code.description: The airport's three-letter FAA code, e.g. 'DFW'.

airport_name.description: The airport's name, e.g. 'Dallas/Ft Worth International'.

average_delay_minutes.description: A ground delay program's average delay, in minutes.

details.description: For a closure, what it covers or exempts, in the notice's words, e.g. 'except HEL' (helicopters) or 'TO NON SKED TRANSIENT GA ACFT'.

end_time.description: When the FAA expects it to end (UTC, ISO 8601): the end of a ground stop or program, or when a closed airport reopens.

event_type.description: What is happening: closure, ground_stop, ground_delay_program, arrival_delay, departure_delay, partial_closure (closed to some flights, such as private planes without permission) or deicing.

event_type_label.description: The kind of event in words, e.g. 'Ground delay program'.

id.description: Names this event: the airport, the kind of event and when it began, e.g. 'DFW|ground_delay_program|2026-10-01T12:00:00Z'. The same event keeps the same id while the FAA lists it, so it is what to compare to tell a new event from one already handled.

in_effect.description: True while the event is under way. False for one the FAA has announced that hasn't started yet, such as a closure tonight.

max_delay_minutes.description: The longest delay, in minutes: a ground delay program's maximum, or the top of an arrival or departure delay's band.

min_delay_minutes.description: An arrival or departure delay's shortest delay, in minutes. The FAA reports these delays as a 15-minute band, e.g. 16 to 30.

notam.description: For a closure, the notice to air missions (NOTAM) that closed the airport, as the FAA published it.

probability_of_extension.description: How likely the FAA thinks a ground stop is to be extended: 'low' (under 30%), 'medium' (30 to 60%) or 'high' (over 60%).

reason.description: Why, as the FAA gives it: the weather or condition behind a ground stop or delay program (e.g. 'Thunderstorms', 'Low ceilings'), or the FAA's code for an arrival or departure delay (e.g. 'TM Initiatives:MIT:VOL'). Empty for closures and deicing.

start_time.description: When it began or begins (UTC, ISO 8601). For a ground delay program, when the program began, even if the FAA has revised it since. Empty for arrival and departure delays.

summary.description: One sentence saying what it means for flights, e.g. 'Ground delay program at Dallas/Ft Worth International (DFW) because of thunderstorms: flights to it are delayed 79 minutes on average and up to 147 minutes, until Oct 2, 02:59 UTC.'

trend.description: Whether an arrival or departure delay is 'increasing' or 'decreasing'.

updated_at.description: When the FAA last updated it (UTC, ISO 8601).

has_delays.description: True when a ground stop, ground delay program or arrival or departure delay is under way there.

latitude.description: The airport's latitude, when the FAA lists it.

longitude.description: The airport's longitude, when the FAA lists it.

status.description: The airport's status, from the most disruptive event under way: closed, ground_stop, ground_delay_program, delays, partially_closed, deicing, or no_delays.

status_label.description: The status in words, e.g. 'Ground stop' or 'No delays'.

summary.description: What is going on, in a sentence for each event, or that the FAA reports no delays there.

get_national_status.description: See every US airport where the FAA is holding up or turning away traffic right now: ground stops, ground delay programs with their average and longest delays, arrival and departure delays and whether they are growing, closures, partial closures and deicing. Each event comes with its airport, reason, start and end times and a sentence saying what it means for flights. Narrow it to the kinds of event you care about. No delays anywhere is an answer, not a failure.

get_operations_plan.description: Read the FAA Command Center's plan for the rest of the day: the ground stops and delay programs it thinks are possible, probable or expected at airports, and the reroutes and route closures it expects en route, each with its time (UTC) and the airports it names. Useful for warning travellers before the delays start.

description: Live US airport delays from the Federal Aviation Administration: ground stops, ground delay programs, arrival and departure delays, closures and deicing at every US airport, one airport's status and runways, the FAA's plan for later in the day, and a trigger for each new delay. No account or API key required.
